mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate compresses equity discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as monetary policy eases.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS trend shows 3-month decline in 70% of cases but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in >40% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: FEDFUNDS exceeding 2.5% for two consecutive months signals aggressive monetary tightening, increasing equity discount rates and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In 80% of FEDFUNDS > 2.5% for 2 consecutive months instances, S&P 500 5-day returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in unemployment rate and rise in nonfarm payrolls indicates labor market strength boosting consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Joint UNRATE decline and PAYEMS rise occurs in 50% of cases but S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in >30% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, rising consumer credit (RSAFS) signals strong household spending that supports corporate earnings, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion regime, RSAFS growth does not correlate with positive 20-day S&P 500 returns (Rank IC < 0.05 over 3-year rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: A 6-month declining unemployment rate trend indicates improving labor market conditions supporting corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE trend shows 6-month decline in 65% of cases but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in >35% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 5.0% for three consecutive months signals economic weakness triggering reduced corporate investment, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In 75% of UNRATE > 5.0% for 3 consecutive months instances, S&P 500 5-day returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in industrial production and rising CPIAUCSL indicates supply shock increasing corporate costs, reducing profit margins and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Joint INDPRO decline and CPIAUCSL rise occurs in 40% of cases but S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in <60% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: During supply shocks, declining industrial production (INDPRO) signals reduced manufacturing output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days as corporate margins compress.
failure_condition: In supply shock regime, INDPRO decline does not predict negative 20-day S&P 500 returns (Rank IC < 0.05 over 3-year rolling windows).
